source.title: Loop, Think, & Generalize: Implicit Reasoning in Recurrent-Depth Transformers
source.authors: Harsh Kohli; Srinivasan Parthasarathy; Huan Sun; Yue-Kun Yao

record.tranche_reason: Tests delayed generalization and its emergence in a controlled synthetic reasoning task, using recurrent-depth transformers and a knowledge-graph composition task rather than the original studies' methods and tasks.
record.gate_note: The paper reports its own training and test accuracy trajectories and mechanistic analyses relevant to grokking. Results cited from prior work are not included. It does not test whether shrinking the training set increases the delay.
record.test_reason: The study reports its own train, ID-test and OOD-test accuracy over training on a synthetic knowledge-graph 2-hop task. OOD accuracy rises long after training accuracy saturates (about 10^4 vs 10^2 epochs). It also tracks bridge and target decodability with logit lens at checkpoints from each stage. This is a new setting (recurrent-depth transformers, compositional reasoning) with direct results on V1 and V2.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is correct. The authors also conclude that recurrent-depth transformers enable depth extrapolation through inference-time recurrence, limited by overthinking.
record.recipe_differences: Uses recurrent-depth transformers trained from scratch on synthetic knowledge-graph multi-hop tasks, rather than the original studies' task and method. The systematicity experiment uses fixed recurrence and analyzes logit-lens decodability and activation-patching effects.
record.method_sensitivity: Systematic generalization varies with training recurrence (R = 1 fails, while recurrent settings generalize); in depth-extrapolation experiments, the authors also report mixed results with default Gaussian rather than zero initialization, but that comparison does not test the grokking versions here.

fits_no_version.finding: Under the depth curriculum, the dynamic-recurrence model needs over 1.3M steps to reach 4-hop, then rapidly generalizes up to 19-hop with few extra steps. This is a phase transition in curriculum progress, not a train/test gap.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Once a compositional rule is discovered, generalization to much deeper compositions follows rapidly (a curriculum phase transition).

record.problems: The evidence is from a single family of structured synthetic reasoning tasks and small-scale models; the authors caution against direct extrapolation to realistic LLMs. Several accuracy values are shown only in figures, and the paper does not vary training-set size.
record.rows_left_out: Section 6 and Appendices F–K report depth-extrapolation, overthinking, initialization, and model-size results, but do not measure the post-overfitting train/test accuracy gap or the gradual mechanism specified by V1–V2. Results cited from other work are also excluded.

untested.parts: Delay growing as the training set shrinks: there is no training-set-size sweep. The text also gives no explicit statement that test accuracy starts at chance or ends near-perfect on the OOD split.
Removal of memorizing components, and a continuous progress measure that quantitatively anticipates the jump. Only three stage checkpoints are analysed.
Not tested. Weight decay is fixed at 0.01, with no critical-size or ungrokking test.

missing.what: The vanilla model exhibits two stages: memorization, then ID generalization (grokking). It never reaches the OOD stage.
Numeric train, ID and OOD accuracy for R = 4 at the stage transitions (final OOD level).
Rapid curriculum phase transition (1.3M steps to 4-hop, then quick progress to 19-hop).

record.verdict_notes: The grokking result is a side finding in a paper on looped transformers. The 'delay' for the systematic split is architecture-dependent. Wang et al. 2024a, the closer prior work, is not an original source here.

versions.untested_parts: No training-set-size sweep; no modular arithmetic table task; no explicit statement that test accuracy starts at chance or becomes near-perfect.
Does not directly measure memorizing components being removed, or show that a continuous progress measure quantitatively anticipates the accuracy jump.
No non-algorithmic data; no test of a lazy-to-rich transition or switching grokking through initialization scale or weight norm.
No realistic large-model pretraining or fine-tuning.
No test of a low-norm efficiency account, critical dataset size, or ungrokking.
Does not compare identifiable algorithms learned across runs.
Does not test whether delayed generalization is caused by adaptive-optimizer instability or floating-point limits in the softmax, or whether controlling those removes it.

rows.subject: vanilla transformer (R = 1)
rows.operation_detail: Train on the synthetic knowledge-graph reasoning task and track test OOD accuracy over epochs.
rows.measure: Test OOD accuracy over training epochs
rows.value: The vanilla transformer completely fails to generalize to unfamiliar atomic-fact compositions.
rows.uncertainty: Figure 3 shading indicates standard deviation; numeric uncertainty not stated.
rows.note: The paper reports failure on OOD compositions regardless of training time.
rows.check: Measures only the OOD split. The vanilla model never generalizes OOD at any training time. Per the text it does grok in-distribution, which no row records.

rows.subject: recurrent-depth transformer (R = 2)
rows.operation_detail: Train on the synthetic knowledge-graph reasoning task and track test OOD accuracy over epochs.
rows.measure: Test OOD accuracy over training epochs
rows.value: Non-trivial generalization; convergence reported at 7k epochs.
rows.uncertainty: Figure 3 shading indicates standard deviation; numeric uncertainty not stated.
rows.note: Non-trivial generalization is reported, but the text does not say this setting reaches near-perfect test accuracy.
rows.check: Only the OOD curve against epochs is reported, with no comparison to train accuracy, so the delay can't be read. Final accuracy is figure-only.

rows.subject: recurrent-depth transformer (R = 4)
rows.operation_detail: Train on the synthetic knowledge-graph reasoning task and track test OOD accuracy over epochs.
rows.measure: Test OOD accuracy over training epochs
rows.value: The model achieves systematic generalization; convergence is reported at 2k epochs.
rows.uncertainty: Figure 3 shading indicates standard deviation; numeric uncertainty not stated.
rows.note: The paper explicitly describes a later systematic-generalization stage after training overfit and in-distribution generalization.
rows.check: Reports convergence speed only (2k epochs), which can't show the train/test delay. The delay for R = 4 is captured by r5–r7; this row largely duplicates them.

rows.measure: Test OOD accuracy over training epochs
rows.uncertainty: Figure 3 shading indicates standard deviation; numeric uncertainty not stated.
rows.note: The text does not separately describe the R = 8 outcome.

rows.subject: recurrent-depth transformer (R = 4)
rows.value: Training accuracy improves while the model overfits the training set.
rows.note: The paper describes training-set overfitting in the first stage.
rows.check: Stage 1: training accuracy rises while test accuracy stays low. This row is the comparison point for the delay.

rows.subject: recurrent-depth transformer (R = 4)
rows.operation_detail: Track in-distribution test accuracy during training.
rows.value: In-distribution generalization emerges after prolonged training beyond memorization; near-perfect in-distribution accuracy precedes systematic generalization.
rows.note: The stated timing comparison is 10^4 vs. 10^2 epochs for systematic generalization versus training overfitting.
rows.check: The authors call in-distribution generalization after prolonged training grokking. The 10^4 vs 10^2 epoch figure in this row's note is actually the OOD (systematic) timing, which belongs to r7.

rows.subject: recurrent-depth transformer (R = 4)
rows.operation_detail: Track test OOD accuracy during training.
rows.value: Systematic generalization arises only in the final stage, after near-perfect in-distribution accuracy.
rows.note: The paper reports the delayed OOD outcome but does not state its numeric accuracy in the text.
rows.check: OOD accuracy rises about 100x later than overfitting (10^4 vs 10^2 epochs). The final OOD value is figure-only, so near-perfection can't be confirmed from the text.

rows.subject: recurrent-depth transformer (R = 2)
rows.operation_detail: Use logit lens to measure bridge-entity and target-entity decodability across effective depth.
rows.measure: Bridge and target entity prediction accuracy at corresponding token positions
rows.value: The model predicts targets without reliably decoding the bridge entity, which the authors characterize as memorization.
rows.note: Evidence for the initial memorization stage; values are presented graphically.
rows.check: Shows the memorization stage: targets are predicted without a decodable bridge. This matches V2's starting point, so the state is observed rather than partial.

rows.subject: recurrent-depth transformer (R = 2)
rows.operation_detail: Use logit lens to measure bridge-entity and target-entity decodability across effective depth.
rows.measure: Bridge and target entity prediction accuracy at corresponding token positions
rows.value: The bridge becomes decodable, followed by correct target prediction for in-distribution data at deeper effective depths.
rows.note: The described sequence is consistent with progressively developing bridge-mediated composition.
rows.check: The bridge becomes decodable in Stage 2, before OOD success. This is an internal change that precedes the OOD jump, but it is shown only at stage checkpoints, not as a continuous measure.

rows.subject: recurrent-depth transformer (R = 2)
rows.operation_detail: Use logit lens to measure bridge-entity and target-entity decodability across effective depth.
rows.measure: Bridge and target entity prediction accuracy at corresponding token positions
rows.value: The model succeeds on OOD inputs only in Stage 3.
rows.note: The paper describes this as the transition to systematic composition.
rows.check: OOD composition appears only in Stage 3.

rows.subject: 8-layer vanilla transformer (R = 1)
rows.operation_detail: Use logit lens to measure bridge-entity and target-entity decodability across effective depth.
rows.value: The vanilla model fails to achieve non-zero systematic generalization regardless of training time.
rows.note: The vanilla model exhibits only two training stages and does not achieve OOD generalization.
rows.check: An 8-layer vanilla model never reaches non-zero OOD accuracy at any training time. This bears on whether delayed generalization arrives (V1), not on V2's gradual-mechanism claim.

source_check.correct: The iso-FLOP eight-layer vanilla transformer has only two training stages and never achieves non-zero systematic generalization; remove the Stage 3 checkpoint designation.
source_check.locator_found: Section 5.2, logit-lens comparison immediately before Figure 4
source_check.problem: The subject specifies Stage 3, but the vanilla model exhibits only two stages.

rows.subject: vanilla transformer
rows.operation_detail: Corrupt the first-hop prefix, restore a clean activation at the r1 position, and measure recovery of the final target prediction.
rows.measure: Bridge and target decodability and causal effect of r1 activations on final r2 logits
rows.value: The bridge is recovered only at much deeper layers (layer 7+), and the target never becomes decodable.
rows.note: The authors interpret the late bridge recovery as too late to support second-hop composition.
rows.check: A causal analysis of why the vanilla model fails OOD. It does not track a circuit forming over training, so it does not bear on V2.

rows.subject: recurrent-depth model
rows.operation_detail: Corrupt the first-hop prefix, restore a clean activation at the r1 position, and measure recovery of the final target prediction.
rows.measure: Causal effect of r1 activations on final r2 logits
rows.value: All layers in the first iteration at position r1 show causal effects on the final answer; subsequent iterations can reuse the rule for the second-hop composition.
rows.note: Supports a recurrent bridge-mediated compositional mechanism; it does not directly show removal of memorizing components.
rows.check: A single Stage-3 snapshot of the causal circuit. It cannot show gradual formation or removal of memorizing components.

relationships.reason: Training overfits by about 10^2 epochs; ID and then OOD generalization arrive much later, about 10^4 epochs (r5, r6, r7).
relationships.display_finding: Training overfit by about 100 epochs, while in-distribution and then out-of-distribution generalization arrived much later, around 10,000 epochs.

source_check.label: supports
source_check.reason: r5–r7 establish training overfitting followed by ID generalization and later OOD generalization; the text compares OOD emergence around 10^4 epochs with overfitting around 10^2.

relationships.condition: Vanilla transformers (4- and 8-layer) on the OOD systematic split
relationships.reason: Delayed generalization never reaches compositions of held-out facts regardless of training time; only ID grokking occurs. Delayed generalization therefore depends on architecture for this split (r1, r11).
relationships.display_finding: Only in-distribution grokking occurred; compositions of held-out facts never generalized across the tested training durations.

relationships.condition: Recurrent-depth transformer (R = 2), logit lens at stage checkpoints

relationships.display_finding: Memorization initially lacks a decodable bridge, which appears in Stage 2 before out-of-distribution success in Stage 3.
